fs-av-angle.front: Which slope angles produce most avalanches?
fs-av-angle.back: 30 to 45 degrees. 25 to 30 less often. Over 45 snow usually sluffs.

fs-av-size.front: How small a slope can still be dangerous?
fs-av-size.back: About 10 m by 10 m can hold enough snow (Avalanche Canada).

fs-av-thin.front: How much snow on a grass or rock slab slope can slide early season?

Yes for goat and sheep hunts in steep alpine terrain in late fall, first snow on grass or rock slabs, gullies used as travel routes, and late season snowmobile access. About 30 centimetres of snow on a smooth slope can slide.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Is this a hunter problem?</text><rect x="30" y="48" width="340" height="42" rx="8" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#4a7fb0" stroke-width="2"/><text x="46" y="75" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start">Goats, sheep</text><text x="200" y="75" font-size="15" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start">steep alpine, late fall</text><rect x="30" y="98" width="340" height="42" rx="8" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#4a7fb0" stroke-width="2"/><text x="46" y="125" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start">First snow</text><text x="200" y="125" font-size="15" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start">on grass or rock slabs</text><rect x="30" y="148" width="340" height="42" rx="8" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#4a7fb0" stroke-width="2"/><text x="46" y="175" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start">Gullies</text><text x="200" y="175" font-size="15" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start">travel routes, traps</text><rect x="30" y="198" width="340" height="42" rx="8" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#4a7fb0" stroke-width="2"/><text x="46" y="225" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start">Snowmobile</text><text x="200" y="225" font-size="15" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start">late season access</text><rect x="15" y="254" width="369" height="30" rx="6" fill="#2f3a2b"/><text x="200" y="275" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff" text-anchor="middle">About 30 cm on a smooth slope can slide</text>
</svg>

fs-av-runout.front: Can an avalanche reach flat ground below?
fs-av-runout.back: Yes. It can run across flat ground and even uphill.

fs-av-traps.back: Gullies or creek beds, cliffs below, trees and rocks in the path, flat ground right below a steep slope.
fs-av-traps.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Terrain traps make an avalanche worse: gullies and creek beds where snow piles deep, cliffs below a slope, trees and rocks in the path, and flat areas right below steep slopes where debris stops. A small slope above a trap can kill.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Terrain traps make it worse</text><rect x="20" y="48" width="170" height="82" rx="10" fill="#fbe9e7" stroke="#c0392b" stroke-width="2"/><text x="105" y="84" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Gully, creek</text><text x="105" y="108" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">snow piles deep</text><rect x="210" y="48" width="170" height="82" rx="10" fill="#fbe9e7" stroke="#c0392b" stroke-width="2"/><text x="295" y="84" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Cliff below</text><text x="295" y="108" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">fall plus burial</text><rect x="20" y="144" width="170" height="82" rx="10" fill="#fbe9e7" stroke="#c0392b" stroke-width="2"/><text x="105" y="180" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Trees, rocks</text><text x="105" y="204" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">trauma in path</text><rect x="210" y="144" width="170" height="82" rx="10" fill="#fbe9e7" stroke="#c0392b" stroke-width="2"/><text x="295" y="180" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Flat below</text><text x="295" y="204" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">debris stops there</text><rect x="46" y="250" width="308" height="30" rx="6" fill="#c0392b"/><text x="200" y="271" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff" text-anchor="middle">Small slope plus a trap can kill</text>
</svg>

fs-av-considerable.front: Which danger level has the most deaths?
fs-av-considerable.back: Considerable (3). Many slopes should be avoided.

fs-av-high.front: Danger rated High: what do you do?
fs-av-high.back: Avoid all avalanche terrain. Mellow slopes or dense trees with no overhead hazard.

fs-av-survival.front: Survival of fully buried people over time?
fs-av-survival.back: Over 90% in the first 15 to 20 minutes, about 35% by 35 minutes. Companion rescue is the best chance.
fs-av-survival.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Survival curve for people fully buried by an avalanche, from Swiss data: over 90 percent alive in the first 15 to 20 minutes, then a steep drop to about 35 percent by 35 minutes. Every minute counts, so your partner is the rescue.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Buried: every minute counts</text><line x1="50" y1="240" x2="370" y2="240" stroke="#2f3a2b" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/><line x1="50" y1="240" x2="50" y2="60" stroke="#2f3a2b" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/><path d="M50 69 L130 74 L157 82 L237 177" fill="none" stroke="#c0392b" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><rect x="50" y="60" width="80" height="180" rx="0" fill="#2e7d32" opacity=".15"/><text x="50" y="260" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">0</text><text x="130" y="260" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">15</text><text x="237" y="260" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">35</text><text x="370" y="260" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">60</text><text x="210" y="280" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">minutes buried</text><text x="44" y="66" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="end">100%</text><text x="44" y="244" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="end">0</text><text x="250" y="70" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d32" text-anchor="middle">Over 90% alive</text><text x="250" y="90" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">in the first 15 to 20 min</text><text x="290" y="190" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#c0392b" text-anchor="middle">About 35%</text><text x="290" y="208" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">by 35 min</text>
